newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian coffee to get EU STABEX funding support.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian coffee to get EU STABEX funding support.

text.p: Tanzania's ailing coffee industry, battling drought and declining production, is likely to receive renewed funding support through the European Union's export earnings stabilisation facility, an EU official said on Tuesday.
"...Funds may be provided under the STABEX instrument in the event of declines in Tanzania's export earnings from specific crops," said EU official Athanassios Theodorakis.

Theodarakis, deputy director-general for the European Commission for Development Cooperation, said the STABEX programme worth 20.8 million Ecus ($24 million) was approved in October 1996. He would not say whether than money had already been disbursed.

Under the programme, the EU allocated compensation payments to farmers totalling 11 million Ecus, 4 million for credit facilities for input stockists, 3 million for secondary road repairs, 1 million for seedling production and 0.8 million for technical training.
Tanzania's coffee production is likely to drop to 41,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 crop season, earning the country an estimated $95 million, according to industry leaders.
Coffee is traditionally Tanzania's biggest earner of foreign exchange. But the East African state has one of the lowest yields of any coffee producer at about 200 kg per hectare.
One reason for the low production figure is the age of its coffee trees, many over 70 years old and well beyond their economic viability, industry leaders say.
